findings.latin: non autem ut illud cui competit esse
findings.suggested: bukan sebagai sesuatu yang memiliki keberadaan itu
findings.why: Latin contrasts esse as received with the subject to which esse belongs; 'sesuatu yang ada' is the glossary rendering of ens and blurs the esse/ens distinction the reply rests on (English 'that which exists').

findings.latin: Perfectum enim dicitur quasi totaliter factum
findings.current: sebab kita menyebut sesuatu sempurna jika ia sudah dibuat secara lengkap
findings.suggested: sebab sesuatu disebut sempurna seakan-akan ia sudah dibuat secara lengkap
findings.why: The objection is etymological (per-factum, 'quasi'), not a condition ('jika'); ad 1 answers exactly this naming by 'transumitur'.

findings.latin: Deus autem ponitur primum principium, non materiale, sed in genere causae efficientis
findings.current: Adapun Allah adalah prinsip pertama, bukan dalam tatanan materi
findings.suggested: Adapun Allah diakui sebagai prinsip pertama, bukan prinsip material, melainkan dalam tatanan sebab efisien
findings.why: 'ponitur' marks a posited premise, and 'non materiale' qualifies the principle, contrasting with the ancients' 'principium materiale'.

findings.latin: non posset ei aliquid deesse de virtute caloris
findings.current: tidak ada sedikit pun dari daya panas yang kurang padanya
findings.suggested: tidak mungkin ada sedikit pun dari daya panas yang kurang padanya
findings.why: The modal 'posset' carries the argument's necessity and is paralleled by 'potest ei deesse' about God in the next sentence.

findings.latin: secundum hoc enim aliqua perfecta sunt, quod aliquo modo esse habent
findings.current: sebab segala sesuatu sempurna justru sejauh ia memiliki keberadaan
findings.suggested: sebab hal-hal sempurna justru sejauh memiliki keberadaan
findings.why: 'aliqua' is indefinite; turning it into 'segala sesuatu' adds a universal quantifier (pelajaran q.1).

findings.latin: totum in seipso uniformiter esse praeaccipit
findings.suggested: sudah lebih dahulu merangkum seluruh keberadaan dalam diri-Nya
findings.why: 'prae-accipit' carries the pre-possession that the whole article argues (praehabet, praeexistere); the English 'embraces' drops it.

findings.latin: illa quae sunt a Deo, assimilantur ei inquantum sunt entia; sicut ipsum esse est commune omnibus
findings.current: semua ciptaan, sejauh semuanya merupakan hal-hal yang ada ...; sebagaimana keberadaan itu umum
findings.suggested: hal-hal yang berasal dari Allah, sejauh semuanya merupakan hal-hal yang ada ...; sebagaimana keberadaan itu sendiri umum
findings.why: Thomas grounds the likeness in the fact that these things come from God as agent ('a Deo'), and 'ipsum esse' is esse itself.

findings.suggested: menurut semacam analogi (dalam arti yang sebagian sama, menurut suatu hubungan)
findings.why: The unified terms require the standard gloss at the first occurrence of 'analogi' in a question.

findings.current: disebut allah karena partisipasi (yaitu karena mengambil bagian dalam keilahian)
findings.suggested: disebut allah melalui partisipasi (mengambil bagian dalam apa yang dimiliki sepenuhnya oleh yang lain)
findings.why: Unified term row D ('melalui partisipasi' plus the standard gloss); this also applies at a3 ad 3.

findings.latin: prout scilicet Deus est ens per essentiam, et alia per participationem
findings.current: sejauh Allah adalah yang ada menurut esensi-Nya, sedangkan hal-hal lain adalah hal-hal yang ada karena partisipasi
findings.suggested: yaitu sejauh Allah adalah yang ada melalui esensi-Nya, sedangkan hal-hal lain adalah hal-hal yang ada melalui partisipasi
findings.why: The unified term is 'melalui partisipasi'; the parallel 'per essentiam' now takes the same preposition, so the contrast stays visible.
Unified term row E: creatura → 'ciptaan' (about 13 occurrences replaced; 'makhluk hidup' for vivens in a2 is kept).

findings.latin: faciamus hominem ad imaginem et similitudinem nostram
findings.suggested: menurut citra dan keserupaan Kita" (Kej 1:26, Vulg.)
findings.why: Unified term row D: imago → 'citra', and Kej 1:26 is marked Vulg. because the argument rests on 'similitudo', where the TB has 'rupa'.

findings.latin: dicimus enim quod imago sit similis homini
findings.current: sebuah gambar serupa dengan seorang manusia
findings.suggested: sebuah citra serupa dengan seorang manusia
findings.why: Unified term row D names q4 a3 ad 4 explicitly: imago → 'citra'.

lessons: [asal: STh I q.4] 'Illud cui competit esse' (the subject that has esse) must not be rendered 'sesuatu yang ada', which is the glossary term for ens; keep the esse/ens distinction visible: 'sesuatu yang memiliki keberadaan itu'.

[asal: STh I q.4] The English 1920 flattens the prae- compounds from Dionysius (praehabet, praeaccipit, praeexistere) into 'embraces'/'contains'. Keep 'sudah lebih dahulu ...' every time, because the argument of a.2 is about pre-existence in the cause.
[asal: STh I q.4] Check the English proper names against the Latin: in a.1 the English has 'Leucippus' where the Latin has 'Speusippus'.
[asal: STh I q.4] 'Quasi' in an etymological definition (perfectum quasi totaliter factum) gives the sense of a name. Render it 'disebut ... seakan-akan', not as a condition with 'jika'.
